user_query:
We’re starting a Phase 2 trial of a GPRC5D‑targeted bispecific antibody in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. The drug is given subcutaneously with step‑up dosing. We want to capture treatment tolerability, CRS symptoms, and patient functioning. Please generate a COA strategy.
HTA markets: NICE, ICER
assumptions_made: population_subtype - no specification of symptomatic vs asymptomatic status
geography - inferred US and EU based on HTA markets NICE and ICER; other regions not mentioned
tpp_domains - based on stated capture goals; other efficacy or symptom domains not specified
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 2

 **In one sentence:** EORTC QLQ-C30 combined with EQ-5D-5L provides the strongest evidence foundation given use in all GPRC5D-targeted bispecific trials and regulatory acceptance for RRMM populations with confirmed psychometric properties [CT-005]. 

 **Key challenge:** Open-label Phase 2 design creates inherent bias risk requiring objective measures to support PRO claims and protocol justification for assessment timing relative to CRS symptoms and step-up dosing [RULE-005][RULE-006]. 

 **Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + EQ-5D-5L based on MonumenTAL-1 precedent [CT-005] satisfies regulatory requirements for sensitive multidimensional HRQoL assessment [RULE-003] with established psychometric properties in RRMM populations [Leleu 2013](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/122/21/1721/12880/Psychometric-Performance-Of-The-EORTC-Quality-Of). 

**Critical gap:** No validated CRS symptom PRO instrument exists for bispecific antibodies — requires novel endpoint development or clinical monitoring integration per [RULE-010].

## Key Observations

- EORTC QLQ-C30 demonstrates consistent sensitivity across all bispecific antibody trials with 5/5 trials showing significant changes in disease-related symptoms [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005]
- EQ-5D-5L provides required HTA utility data with established MCID (0.075) for multiple myeloma patients [Chen 2025](https://hqlo.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12955-025-02383-x) and regulatory acceptance [TI-001]
- CRS symptom assessment represents critical unmet measurement need with no validated PRO instruments available across all comparator trials [Table 1]  
- MonumenTAL-1 provides direct GPRC5D-targeted precedent using EORTC QLQ-C30 + EQ-5D-5L combination with positive regulatory outcomes [CT-005]
- Translation limitations create operational risks with EORTC QLQ-MY20 (1 language) and MySIm-Q (1 language) requiring immediate linguistic validation [Table 5]
- Open-label bias concerns require objective clinical correlation per EMA guidance for symptom-based endpoints [RULE-005]

## Comparator Analysis

MAIA established EORTC QLQ-C30 + EQ-5D-5L as the reference standard for CD38-targeted agents, demonstrating significant improvements in global health status and pain with quarterly assessments [CT-001]. ICARIA-MM confirmed EORTC QLQ-C30 sensitivity for pain, fatigue, and physical functioning using monthly assessments in the same indication [CT-002]. AQUILA replicated these findings with modified timing schedules showing sustained sensitivity [CT-003]. MajesTEC-1 first demonstrated EORTC QLQ-C30 + EQ-5D-5L utility in BCMA-directed bispecifics with significant improvements maintained through 12 cycles [CT-004]. MonumenTAL-1 provides the most relevant precedent as the only GPRC5D-targeted bispecific trial, confirming EORTC QLQ-C30 + EQ-5D-5L sensitivity with addition of PGIS for side effect assessment [CT-005]. EORTC QLQ-C30 emerges as the single best-supported instrument for disease-related symptoms measurement based on universal use and consistent efficacy across the bispecific antibody drug class [CT-001][CT-002][CT-003][CT-004][CT-005].

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument & Version | Preferred Value Set | Current Battery Status | Risk if Omitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | England 5L value set | In candidates | QALY calculation impossible; NICE will issue a Request for Additional Data, delaying reimbursement by ≥12 months |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | US value set | In candidates | Cost-effectiveness analysis not possible; ICER may downgrade evidence rating due to missing utility data |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to add EORTC QLQ-MY20 for treatment tolerability capture given Table 1 shows no candidates for this TPP domain, but only 1 language available requiring immediate translation commissioning (Table 5) versus relying on QLQ-C30 subscales per [RULE-008] validation requirements.

2. Assessment frequency for step-up dosing: adopt MonumenTAL-1 schedule (Screening; C1D1; every 2 cycles D1) versus intensive CRS monitoring schedule (Screening; Step-up doses; C1D1; weekly for 4 weeks; then every 2 cycles) to capture acute tolerability per [RULE-006] timing justification requirements.

3. CRS symptom measurement approach: develop novel symptom diary integrated with clinical CRS grading versus expand EORTC QLQ-C30 symptom items with additional questions, given Table 1 shows no validated PRO candidates and [RULE-010] requires early scientific advice for novel methodologies.

4. Primary PRO endpoint selection: pre-specify global health status (QLQ-C30) as key secondary given MonumenTAL-1 precedent [CT-005] versus physical functioning given consistent sensitivity across all 5 bispecific trials, requiring [RULE-001] scientific rationale documentation.

5. Multiplicity control strategy: include both EORTC QLQ-C30 and EQ-5D-5L in formal statistical hierarchy versus designate EQ-5D-5L as HTA-supportive only to avoid [RULE-002] alpha inflation while maintaining NICE/ICER submission capability.
